Younus Bhuiya (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bashati Property Development Ltd and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 26. Dr M Zahir along with Mr AKM Nazrul Islam, the learned Advocates appearing for the respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 submit that 3rd Annual General Meeting of the Company was held on 6th April, 1994 at the Company's registered Office which was attended by all the shareholders/Directors and in that meeting resolution was taken that Moqbul Ahmed was appointed as Managing Director for the next 3 years. Mrs Maksuda Ahmed proposed the re-appointment, and the proposal was seconded by the petitioner Younus Bhuiyan and the proposal was accepted unanimously. He submits that Far East Property Development was registered on 9-4-1994, Registration No. being 28150. The Company is carrying on business for developing and selling the land of Bashati Property Development Ltd as per Tripartite Agreement dated 19-6-1992. He stated that respondent No. 4 filed a Criminal Case being GR Case No. 349 of 1995 arising out of Mirpur PS Case No. 21 dated 6-2-1995 only to harass the respondent No. 2 and the aforesaid case was quashed by the High Court Division. Thereafter, the present petitioner and the respondent No. 4 filed Company Matter No. 17 of 1995 under section 233 of the Companies Act which was dismissed on the ground of maintainability. Then the respondent No. 4 filed Company Matter No. 101 of 1997 which was subsequently withdrawn by the respondent No. 4 and finally so far the present Company Matter No. 15 of 1998 was filed by the present petitioner for winding up of the Company which is a running Company and is doing good business. So, it is apparent that the so-called deadlock was created not for the benefit of the Company respondent No. 1, but for the benefit of Far East Property Development Limited. He submits that the systematic course of conduct of the present petitioner and his brother respondent No. 4 shows that they were actuated by malice which is malice in law and, as such, the winding up petition not being a bonafide one is liable to be missed. He further submits that the Tripartite Agreement was executed on 19th June, 1992 relating to lands described in schedules 'Ka' lha"gas between late Md Nazmul Huda and his heirs as first party and Bashati Property Development Limited ac second party and Maksuder Rahman respondent No. 4 a shareholder/Director of Bashati Property Development Limited, Maqbul Ahmed, Md Jahangir Alam and Md Shahadat Hossain as 3rd party. Other petitioner of this matter is the brother Muksudur Rahman respondent No.4 who in collusion with the heirs of late Md Nazmul Huda and in breach of the terms and conditions of the tripartite agreement in question designed by secret machinations to deprive the Company of 6 acres of land of the Company. Under these compelling situations the Company has been forced to institute Title Suit No.15 of 1998 in Court of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Dhaka with a prayer for a decree for executing 6 acres of land out of the total land comprising Schedules 'Ka', 'Kha' and 'Ga' of the tripartite Agreement. He submits that respondent No.4 in breach of faith and fiduciary duties towards the present Company has acted contrary to the interest of the present Company and, as such, the winding up petition should not be allowed. Article 80 of the Articles of Association of the Company provides for arbitration for any dispute and, as such, it is submitted that the winding up petition is liable to be dismissed.
